teaser.en: A sprawling seashore shrub whose glossy leaves lather like soap when rubbed in water.

summary.en: Msuko is Colubrina asiatica, a scrambling shrub of beach thickets and the edges of mangroves. Pakia records only its Digo name.

about.en: Msuko is a sprawling or climbing shrub with long, flexible, zig-zag branches. Its leaves are alternate, egg-shaped, shiny bright green and finely toothed, with three main veins. The tiny greenish-yellow flowers are clustered in the leaf angles and are followed by small round capsules that split into three when dry.

where.en: It grows just behind the beach, in coastal thicket, on coral rock and on the landward edges of mangroves. Its seeds float, which is how it has spread along tropical coasts from Africa to the Pacific.

uses.en: Pakia records no Digo use. Elsewhere around the Indian Ocean and Pacific the leaves, which are rich in saponins, are well known for lathering in water and are used as a soap substitute.

names.en: Pakia records the Digo name Msuko but gives no meaning or shared names. The same name is used for Grewia holstii (also called Msokoto). In English it is Asian nakedwood or latherleaf; its scientific name is Colubrina asiatica.

reason.en: Another shrub of the beach thicket
Also grows at the mangrove's landward edge
